name: Pointwise power-law remap (white, grey, velvet, violet, PowerNoiseSuite)
plain: Despite the color names, these transform each sample's value and leave the spectrum flat. They change the histogram of the noise: with alpha near 0 values go toward ±1, with larger alpha the tails get heavier.
math:
white: sign(n)·|n|^α·scale (default α=0, so ±scale).
grey: n·|n|^(α−1)·scale (default α=1, so Gaussian).
velvet: sign(n)·|n|^(1/α)/max|·|.
violet: sign(n)·|n|^(α/2)/max|·|.

props.normalizes_variance: no in PowerNoiseSuite; yes in sonar

providers.author: blepping
providers.note: sign(n) or n times |n|^α, optional divide by max, normalized by scale_noise. Named variants: white α=0 sign (so ±1), grey α=0 no sign (Gaussian), velvet α=1 sign (Gaussian÷max then renormalized, effectively Gaussian), violet α=.5 sign. See noise.py:2286.

label: from code
surprise: Sonar's 'white' is ±1 only (sign(n)·|n|⁰), and sonar's 'velvet' reduces to Gaussian since sign(n)·|n| = n.
